paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the law was never the problem. Paul says it plainly, "the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good" (Romans 7:12). The trouble is what sin does with a good commandment, because sin takes the opportunity and goes to work (Romans 7:8). So when you feel stuck under a rule you can't keep, don't blame the rule. The rule is doing its job.

And what is that job? Paul says it was "in order that sin might be exposed as sin" (Romans 7:13). The law is like a flashlight in a dark kitchen: it shows you the crumbs, but it was never going to sweep them up. It can tell you the truth about yourself, but it can't rescue you from it. That's why it matters to you, because you can stop trying to be your own rescue.

So who does the rescuing? Paul says believers "died to the law through the body of Christ, that you might belong to another, to Him who was raised from the dead" (Romans 7:4). You're released, and you belong to Jesus now. You serve "in the new way of the Spirit, and not in the old way of the written code" (Romans 7:6). I sat in a drawer thinking my story was over, and I'm telling you, belonging to the One who raises the dead beats every checklist there is. Go bear fruit for God, baker.
